A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 34-page versions of the same research work. Corresponding text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on CIFAR-20, CelebA-HQ, and ArtBench, including attribution accuracy, runtime, counterfactual evaluations, and supplementary analyses in Appendices D and F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main comparisons in Table 1 and the experimental results throughout Appendices D and F.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same KernelSHAP estimation framework, model pruning, full-data fine-tuning, and subsequent contributor-subset fine-tuning. The objectives, model components, and inference procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image quality on CIFAR-20, demographic diversity on CelebA-HQ, and aesthetic quality on ArtBench Post-Impressionism. The datasets, contributor populations, and counterfactual test scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in Table 1 and Appendix F is unchanged, including similarity methods, influence functions, TRAK variants, and leave-one-out. The supplementary Banzhaf, alternative Shapley implementation, and unlearning comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: Model sizes, fine-tuning budgets, metrics, subset sizes, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Section 4.5 now calls alpha = 0.25 and 0.75 additional settings, while alpha = 0.5 remains in Table 1. Removing explicit pruning ratios does not establish a changed experimental setting.

E4.justification: Appendix D retains the fine-tuning-step analyses. Appendix F retains the subset-count and computational-budget comparisons, generated-image examples, alternative unlearning evaluations, top-contributor analyses, and data-quality distributions.

E5.justification: Section 4.4 retains means and 95% confidence intervals across three independent sets of 100 held-out subsets. The tables retain their reporting practices, including Table 12's confidence intervals across 100 sampled Shapley subsets.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains the proposed method's LDS results of 61.48 ± 2.27, 26.34 ± 3.42, and 61.44 ± 2.04 for the three datasets.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–2, Propositions 1–2, their assumptions, and the lemmas and proofs in Appendix A are unchanged. Changing the counterfactual contributor-count notation from k to K is mathematically equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions: attributing global diffusion-model properties to contributors, making Shapley estimation feasible through pruning and fine-tuning, and demonstrating advantages over existing attribution methods.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 softens the assertion that high-quality labeling ensures clear, meaningful objects to an expectation that it should do so. Section 5 removes the proposed Owen-value extension for allocating contributor importance to individual data points. Other interpretations and limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page footnote identifying the authors' code repository. Section 4.2 removes the explicit pruning ratios of 0.3 for CIFAR-20 and 0.5 for CelebA-HQ and ArtBench, while retaining the resulting parameter counts. Other implementation and hardware details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 removes the discussion of the Owen value and the corresponding Owen (1977) reference. The remaining related-work coverage and positioning against existing diffusion-model attribution methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 tightens the discussion, clarifies several sentences, corrects citation punctuation, expands author contact information, and adds acknowledgements. The overall section sequence and most prose, including the appendices, are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds ICLR 2025 publication headers, adjusts page flow and Table 1 placement, and reduces or repositions Figures 1, 2, and 4. Figure and table membership, plotted content, captions, and appendix displays are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The new code-access footnote provides a useful implementation pointer absent from v2, and limited wording edits improve clarity and qualify one interpretation. Removing explicit pruning ratios slightly weakens implementation documentation, although parameter counts remain. With the scientific evidence unchanged, the net gain is limited to accessibility and presentation.
